req.title: Posts include author username
req.statement: The system shall join post rows with users so index/detail responses include the author's username.

doc.reasoning: The requirement mandates that GET / joins post rows with users and returns the author's username in the response. Tests must verify: (1) positive — the pre-loaded post's author username 'test' appears in the index response alongside the post title; (2) negative — a post whose author_id has no matching user row is excluded (JOIN semantics, not LEFT JOIN); (3) boundary — exactly one post exists in the fixture, so the response contains exactly one username occurrence tied to that post, and a second user ('other') with no posts does NOT appear as an author on the index. Additional tests cover the exact SQL columns selected (id, title, body, created, author_id, username) and that the HTTP status is exactly 200.

tests.name: test_index_returns_200_with_author_username
preconditions: Database pre-loaded with user id=1 username='test' and post id=1 author_id=1 title='test title'
App created with TESTING=True and isolated temp database
actions: Send GET / with the Flask test client
expected: HTTP status code is exactly 200
Response body contains b'test title'
Response body contains b'test' (the author username)
trace: R-FLASKR-024: index response must include author username via JOIN
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()
r = client.get('/')
assert r.status_code == 200
assert b'test title' in r.data
assert b'test' in r.data

tests.name: test_index_post_without_matching_user_excluded_by_inner_join
preconditions: A post is inserted with a non-existent author_id (orphan row)
actions: Insert a post with author_id=999 (no matching user row)
Send GET / with the Flask test client
expected: HTTP status code is exactly 200
Response body does NOT contain b'orphan title' (INNER JOIN excludes unmatched posts)
trace: R-FLASKR-024: SQL uses INNER JOIN so posts with no matching user are excluded
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()
    db = get_db()
    db.execute(
        "INSERT INTO post (title, body, author_id, created) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
        ('orphan title', 'orphan body', 999, '2024-01-01 00:00:00')
    )
    db.commit()

client = app.test_client()
r = client.get('/')
assert r.status_code == 200
assert b'orphan title' not in r.data

tests.name: test_index_exactly_one_post_one_username_in_fixture
preconditions: Database pre-loaded with exactly 1 post authored by user 'test'
actions: Send GET / with the Flask test client
Count occurrences of the post title and author username in the response

b'test title' appears at least once in response
b'test\nbody' or b'test' appears in response confirming join data present

A second post is inserted authored by user id=2 'other'
